  • Explosive First Step

  • Resisted sprints with bands (10 yards, 4 sets)
  • Falling starts to sprint (3 sets of 5 each direction)

  • Box drill with explosive exits (4 corners)

  • Rotational Power

  • Med ball slams: 3 sets of 15
  • Rotational cable pushes: 3 sets of 12 each side
  • Russian twists with weight: 3 sets of 20

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Return and Attack (20 minutes)
  • Focus on taking short serves and attacking immediately
  • Approach shots off weak returns

  • Practice volley after aggressive return

  • Consistency Under Pressure (15 minutes)

  • Target depth: aim for last 3 feet of court
  • Consecutive in-play returns goal (e.g., 20 in a row)
  • Simulate break points: must make return to win point

docs.title: Week 3-4 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Tuesday: Reaction + Explosiveness (90 min)
  • Thursday: Recognition + Positioning (75 min)
  • Saturday: Attacking Returns + Consistency (90 min)
  • Sunday: Match Play Simulation (60 min) - focus on aggressive second serve returns

docs.title: Goals: Perform under match pressure, develop return strategies based on server tendencies
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Pattern Recognition and Anticipation (20 minutes)
  • Study opponent's serving patterns (deuce vs ad, first vs second serve)
  • Develop "if-then" plans based on serve location and type

  • Practice disguising your return intentions until last moment

  • Advanced Return Techniques (15 minutes)

  • Block return for heavy serves (minimal backswing)
  • Chip and charge for second serves

  • Swinging volley off high bouncing serves

  • Mental Routines (10 minutes)

  • Pre-serve routine: feet positioning, grip adjustment, focus point
  • Between-points routines to stay focused
  • Managing frustration on missed returns

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Repeat Sprint Ability
  • 300-yard shuttles (6x50 yards) with short rest
  • Tabata intervals: 20 seconds on/10 seconds off for 4 minutes (agility ladder or sprints)

  • Hill sprints: 8x20 seconds uphill walk down

  • Core Endurance

  • Plank variations: front, side, reverse (3 sets of 45 seconds each)
  • Hanging knee raises: 3 sets of 20

  • Pallof press: 3 sets of 15 each side

  • Injury Prevention

  • Eccentric heel drops for Achilles: 3 sets of 15
  • External rotations with bands: 3 sets of 20
  • Scapular wall slides: 3 sets of 15

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Match Simulation Returns (25 minutes)
  • Play return games: return serve only, server gets point if you miss return
  • Serve and return sets: first to 6 games, but only return points count

  • Practice returning under different score situations (love-40, deuce, ad-in/out)

  • Strategic Application (15 minutes)

  • Practice specific return strategies against different server types:
    • Big server: block deep, look for second serve to attack
    • Spin specialist: take on the rise, use pace
    • Lefty serve: adjust positioning and swing path

docs.title: Week 5-6 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Pattern Recognition + Repeat Sprints (90 min)
  • Wednesday: Advanced Techniques + Core (75 min)
  • Friday: Match Simulations + Strategy (90 min)
  • Sunday: Practice Match (90 min) - focus on implementing return game plan

docs.title: Phase 4: Match Play Integration and Maintenance (Weeks 7-10)
Goals: Integrate return game into overall match strategy, maintain and refine skills
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Return in Context of Point Construction (20 minutes)
  • Practice using return to set up forehand
  • Develop patterns: return crosscourt, move to net, volley

  • Practice using return to neutralize and restart point

  • Advanced Tactical Situations (15 minutes)

  • Returning serve-and-volley opponents
  • Returning in doubles (positioning, communication)

  • Returning second serves with aggression and variety

  • Video Analysis and Self-Review (10 minutes)

  • Review match footage of your returns
  • Compare to Agassi's technique and decision making
  • Identify one area to improve each week

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Maintenance Phase
  • Reduce volume, maintain intensity
  • Focus on injury prevention and recovery

  • Continue agility and reaction work at reduced volume

  • Peak Performance Preparation

  • Taper training volume in final week before competition
  • Maintain sharpness with short, focused sessions
  • Prioritize sleep, nutrition, and hydration

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Full Match Play (25 minutes)
  • Play practice sets and matches
  • Focus on implementing return game plan

  • Track return statistics: % made, % aggressive points won, break points converted

  • Cool-down and Reflection (10 minutes)

  • Static stretching for legs, shoulders, back
  • Brief journaling on what worked and what to improve

docs.title: Week 7-10 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Mondays: Technique + Video Analysis (75 min)
  • Wednesdays: Tactical Situations + Maintenance Fitness (75 min)
  • Fridays: Match Play (90 min)
  • Sundays: Light Session + Recovery (60 min) or Match Play

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 1-6 Example)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Technique + Agility 90 min Wednesday Positioning + Plyometrics 75 min Friday Direction Control + Core 90 min Sunday Match Play Simulation 60 min

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 7-10 Example)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Technique + Video Analysis 75 min Wednesday Tactical Situations + Maintenance Fitness 75 min Friday Match Play 90 min Sunday Light Session + Recovery 60 min

docs.title: Split Step and Reaction
docs.text:
1. Shadow Split to Serve: Practice split step timing to shadow serve motion
  2. Toss Call: Partner serves, you call out toss location before contact
  3. Reaction Ball Shuffle: Shuffle laterally, catch reaction ball after bounce
  4. Light Sprint to Cone: React to visual cue, sprint to designated cone

docs.title: Positioning and Movement
docs.text:
1. Baseline to Target: Start at baseline, move to touch cone, recover to base
  2. Diagonal Recovery: Hit shadow return, recover to ideal position for next shot
  3. In-and-Out Steps: Practice moving forward for short serves, back for deep
  4. Shadow Return and Recover: Full motion return, then recover to center

docs.title: Direction and Depth Control
docs.text:
1. Cone Alley: Aim returns between two cones placed at baseline
  2. Depth Ladder: Hit to progressively deeper zones (short, medium, deep)
  3. Crosscourt/Down-the-Line Alternation: Alternate directions with each shot
  4. Target Pyramid: Hit to specific targets in sequence (wide, body, T, wide)

docs.title: Pressure and Match Play
docs.text:
1. Return Game: Play games where only return points count
  2. Break Point Simulation: Serve at 0-40, you must break to win game
  3. Consistency Challenge: See how many returns you can make in a row
  4. Score Situation Returns: Practice returning at specific scores (30-40, ad-in, etc.)

docs.title: Agility and Reaction Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 3-4 times per week
  • Intensity: High effort, short duration (10-20 seconds per bout)
  • Recovery: Full recovery between bouts (40-60 seconds rest)
  • Progression: Increase complexity before increasing duration

docs.title: Strength and Power Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 2-3 times per week
  • Intensity: Moderate to high (60-85% 1RM equivalent)
  • Volume: 2-4 sets of 8-15 repetitions
  • Progression: Increase resistance before increasing volume

docs.title: Endurance Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 2 times per week
  • Type: Interval-based (mimics tennis work-rest ratios)
  • Example: 30 seconds high intensity/90 seconds active recovery x 8-10

docs.title: Weekly Metrics to Track
docs.text:
1. Return Percentage: % of serves returned in play (overall, first serve, second serve)
  2. Aggressive Return Percentage: % of returns that are offensive (approach shot, winner, forced error)
  3. Break Points Converted: % of break point opportunities won
  4. Return Points Won: % of points won when returning serve
  5. Unforced Errors on Return: % of return errors that are unforced

docs.title: Monthly Assessment
docs.text:
1. Video Analysis: Compare technique to baseline video
  2. Match Statistics: Track return performance in practice matches
  3. Physical Testing:
  4. 10-yard sprint time
  5. Pro-agility time
  6. Vertical jump height
  7. Medicine ball throw distance
  8. Subjective Rating: Rate your confidence returning serve (1-10 scale)

docs.title: Beginner Focus (NTRP 2.5-3.5)
docs.text:
• Weeks 1-2: Extended focus on split step and basic positioning
  • Weeks 3-4: Slower pace serves, emphasis on making contact
  • Weeks 5-6: Introduction to direction control with larger targets
  • Weeks 7-10: Game-based situations, focus on consistency over aggression

docs.title: Intermediate Focus (NTRP 4.0-4.5)
docs.text:
• Standard progression as outlined above
  • Emphasis: Developing aggressive return options
  • Adjustment: Increase serve speed gradually

docs.title: Advanced Focus (NTRP 5.0+)
docs.text:
• Accelerated timeline: 6-8 week program possible
  • Emphasis: Tactical variations and pressure performance
  • Adjustment: Incorporate opponent-specific strategies and scouting

docs.title: Senior/Injury-Return Focus
docs.text:
• Reduced Impact: Substitute jumping with step movements
  • Increased Recovery: Longer rest intervals, additional recovery days
  • Focus: Precision and placement over explosive movement
  • Equipment: Use of softer balls, smaller court if needed

docs.title: Integration with Overall Game
docs.text:
• Serve Game: Use strong return to break serve and reduce pressure on your own service games
  • Baseline Play: Develop transitions from return to baseline rallies
  • Net Play: Practice approaching the net after strong returns
  • Mental Game: Develop routines to stay focused and positive during return games

docs.title: Coach's Notes
docs.text:
• Individualization: Adjust based on player's age, physique, and return style (blocker vs. puncher)
  • Video Feedback: Use delayed video or live feedback for immediate correction
  • Patience: Return improvements take consistent practice; expect 6-8 weeks for noticeable changes
  • Fun and Engagement: Incorporate games and challenges to maintain motivation
  • Holistic Development: Return is crucial but ensure balanced development of all skills

docs.title: Safety Considerations
docs.text:
• Warm-up: Always complete dynamic warm-up before intense reaction work
  • Cool-down: Static stretching for hips, legs, shoulders, and back after sessions
  • Hydration: Maintain proper fluid intake, especially during intense sessions
  • Surface: Be aware of court conditions; slippery surfaces increase injury risk
  • Equipment: Use appropriate footwear with good lateral support

docs.title: References & Resources
docs.text:
• Video Study: Andre Agassi return highlights (1990s US Open, Australian Open)
  • Books: "Andre Agassi: Open" (autobiography), tennis technique texts
  • Coaching Aids: USPTA/PTR return of serve development materials
  • Technology: Reaction lights, high-speed cameras for analysis if available

Program developed based on analysis of Andre Agassi's return technique, training methodologies, and match performance data. Adapt volume, intensity, and focus based on individual athlete needs, age, and competitive level. Consult with qualified tennis coach and fitness professional before beginning any intensive training program.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This training program is designed to develop the flexibility, elasticity, and adaptive capabilities that define Novak Djokovic's legendary durability and ability to perform at the highest level across all surfaces and conditions. The program focuses on elastic strength, dynamic flexibility, joint mobility, and the mental flexibility to adapt tactics mid-match.

docs.title: Program Overview
docs.text:
• Duration: 12 weeks (can be adjusted based on athlete level)
  • Frequency: 5-6 sessions per week (mix of on-court, flexibility, and mental training)
  • Session Length: 75-105 minutes (flexibility work daily, on-court every other day)
  • Equipment Needed: Tennis court, balls, yoga mat, resistance bands, foam roller, massage ball, yoga blocks, stability ball, meditation app/guide, video analysis equipment
  • Prerequisites: Basic tennis fundamentals, no serious joint limitations, willingness to commit to daily flexibility work

docs.title: Philosophy & Approach
docs.text: Djokovic's physical and mental game is built on: 1. Elasticity & Reactive Strength: Ability to store and release energy efficiently in movements 2. Exceptional Flexibility & Range of Motion: Particularly in hips, shoulders, and spine 3. Joint Health & Injury Prevention: Focus on durability and longevity 4. Mental Flexibility & Adaptability: Ability to change strategies and stay present under pressure 5. Recovery & Regeneration: Systematic approach to recovery between sessions and matches

docs.title: Goals: Establish baseline flexibility, develop daily routine, introduce elastic strength concepts
Daily Flexibility Routine (Non-Negotiable - 20 minutes daily)
docs.text:
• Morning Routine (10 minutes upon waking)
  • Neck rolls: 10 each direction
  • Shoulder circles: 15 forward, 15 backward
  • Arm swings: 20 each direction
  • Torso twists: 20 each side
  • Hip circles: 15 each direction

  • Leg swings (front-back, side-side): 15 each leg each direction

  • Evening Routine (10 minutes post-training or before bed)

  • Child's pose: 2 minutes
  • Cat-cow stretch: 2 minutes
  • Pigeon pose: 1 minute each side
  • Seated forward fold: 2 minutes
  • Supine twist: 1 minute each side
  • Legs up wall: 2 minutes
  • Savasana/deep breathing: 2 minutes

docs.title: Joint Mobility & Activation (3x/week, 15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Ankle Mobility (5 minutes)
  • Ankle circles: 20 each direction each ankle
  • Dorsiflexion/plantarflexion walks: 20 steps

  • Tibial raises: 2x15

  • Hip Mobility (5 minutes)

  • 90/90 switches: 2 minutes
  • Hip circles: 10 each direction each leg

  • Deep squat hold: 2 minutes (accumulated)

  • Shoulder & Thoracic Mobility (5 minutes)

  • Wall slides: 2x15
  • Thoracic rotations on foam roller: 2 minutes
  • Doorway pec stretch: 1 minute each side
  • Scapular push-ups: 2x15

docs.title: Elastic Strength Introduction (2x/week, 20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Pogo Jumps (ankle stiffness)
  • Two-foot: 3x20 seconds
  • Single-leg alternating: 3x15 each leg

  • Lateral: 3x15 each side

  • Medicine Ball Elasticity

  • Chest pass against wall (focus on quick release): 3x15
  • Overhead throw (focus on stretch-shortening cycle): 3x10
  • Rotational throws (focus on hip-shoulder separation): 3x10 each side

docs.title: On-Court Application (2x/week, 30 minutes)
docs.text:
• Dynamic Warm-up Before Hitting
  • Ladder drills with varied patterns: 5 minutes
  • Carioca with arm swings: 2 minutes each direction

  • Backpedal to sprint transitions: 5x10 yards

  • Flexibility-Integrated Drills

  • Shadow swings with full range of motion: 5 minutes
  • Service motion focus on shoulder flexibility: 10 minutes
  • Groundstroke swings emphasizing hip rotation: 10 minutes
  • Volley practice with low, wide base: 5 minutes

docs.title: Week 1-3 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Flexibility AM/PM + Joint Mobility AM + Elastic Strength PM
  • Tuesday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application AM
  • Wednesday: Flexibility AM/PM + Joint Mobility PM + Elastic Strength AM
  • Thursday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application PM
  • Friday: Flexibility AM/PM + Joint Mobility AM + Elastic Strength PM
  • Saturday: Flexibility AM/PM + Light On-Court (focus on technique)
  • Sunday: Flexibility AM/PM + Active Recovery (walk, swim, yoga)

docs.title: Goals: Increase range of motion, develop elastic strength in tennis-specific movements, begin mental flexibility training
Enhanced Daily Flexibility (25-30 minutes daily)
docs.text:
• Morning Routine (15 minutes)
  • Sun Salutations A & B: 3 rounds each
  • Dynamic leg swings with torso rotation: 10 each leg each direction
  • Scorpion stretches: 10 each side
  • World's greatest stretch: 5 each side

  • Deep squat with torso rotations: 1 minute

  • Evening Routine (15 minutes)

  • Pigeon pose variations: 2 minutes each side
  • Frog stretch: 2 minutes
  • Butterfly stretch: 2 minutes
  • Seated wide-legged forward fold: 2 minutes
  • Supine hamstring stretch with strap: 2 minutes each leg
  • Thread the needle: 1 minute each side
  • Savasana/deep breathing: 3 minutes

docs.title: Tennis-Specific Flexibility (3x/week, 20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Serving Shoulder Flexibility
  • Sleeper stretch: 2x30 seconds each side
  • Doorway pec stretch with rotation: 2x30 seconds each side
  • Lat hang on bar: 2x30 seconds

  • External rotation with band: 2x15 each side

  • Hip Flexibility for Groundstrokes

  • 90/90 hip switches with reach: 2 minutes
  • Dynamic pigeon walks: 2 minutes
  • Lateral lunges with reach: 2x10 each side

  • Cossack squats: 2x10 each side

  • Spinal Rotation & Extension

  • Thread the needle with reach: 2x30 seconds each side
  • Cobra to child's pose flow: 2 minutes
  • Seated spinal twist: 2x30 seconds each side
  • Cat-cow with exaggerated range: 2 minutes

docs.title: Elastic Strength & Power (3x/week, 20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Low-Load, High-Velocity Exercises
  • Jump rope variations: 5 minutes (single-leg, double-unders, side-to-side)
  • Medicine ball chest pass (focus on speed): 3x20
  • Medicine ball overhead throw (focus on stretch reflex): 3x15

  • Lateral bounds with quick ground contact: 3x15 each side

  • Reactive Strength Intervals

  • 10 seconds on/20 seconds off: pogo jumps, lateral bounds, squat jumps
  • 4 sets of 4 minutes

docs.title: Mental Flexibility Training (Daily, 10-15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Mindfulness & Presence
  • Morning meditation: 5-10 minutes (focus on breath, body scan)

  • Between-point routine practice: 5 minutes (visualize routines)

  • Adaptability Scenarios (3x/week)

  • Visualize different match scenarios (wind, rain, slow/fast courts)
  • Practice changing game plans mid-point in visualization
  • Develop "if-then" plans for common opponent patterns

docs.title: On-Court Application (3x/week, 30 minutes)
docs.text:
• Flexibility-Integrated Drills
  • Extreme wide balls: focus on loading and exploding from stretched position
  • Low balls: emphasize getting down and using full leg extension
  • High balls: focus on spinal extension and shoulder flexibility

  • Transition shots: practice moving from extreme positions to balanced recovery

  • Point Construction with Variety

  • Practice constructing points using different spins and trajectories
  • Work on changing patterns mid-rally based on hypothetical opponent adjustments

docs.title: Week 4-6 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Flexibility AM/PM + Tennis-Specific Flex AM + Elastic Strength PM + Mental Training
  • Tuesday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application AM + Tennis-Specific Flex PM
  • Wednesday: Flexibility AM/PM + Elastic Strength AM + Mental Training PM
  • Thursday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application PM + Tennis-Specific Flex AM
  • Friday: Flexibility AM/PM + Elastic Strength AM + Mental Training PM
  • Saturday: Flexibility AM/PM + Light On-Court (match simulation focus)
  • Sunday: Flexibility AM/PM + Active Recovery + Extended Meditation (20 min)

docs.title: Goals: Integrate flexibility and elasticity into match play, develop consistency under fatigue, refine mental adaptability
Maintenance Flexibility (20-25 minutes daily)
docs.text:
• Morning Routine (12 minutes)
  • Flow sequence: Sun A + Warrior II sequence + balance poses
  • Dynamic hip opener series: 5 minutes

  • Shoulder mobility complex: 3 minutes

  • Evening Routine (10-13 minutes)

  • Targeted stretching based on day's tension (use foam roller first)
  • PNF stretching for major muscle groups (hold-contract-relax)
  • Breathing exercises: 4-7-8 pattern for 2 minutes

docs.title: Tennis-Specific Elasticity (3x/week, 20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Serve Elasticity Focus
  • Trophy position holds with perturbations: 3x15 seconds each side
  • Medicine ball slams from serve position: 3x10

  • Jump serve practice focusing on stretch-shortening cycle: 15 minutes

  • Groundstroke Elasticity

  • Open stance loading drills: 3x15 each side (focus on hip stretch reflex)
  • Closed stance step-through drills: 3x15 each side

  • Recovery jumps after wide shots: 3x10 each direction

  • Movement Elasticity

  • Split-step reaction with varied timing: 5 minutes
  • Lateral shuffle to sprint with immediate direction change: 4x20 seconds
  • Drop step and recover: 3x10 each direction

docs.title: Advanced Mental Flexibility (Daily, 15-20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Match Simulation Visualization
  • Pre-match routine visualization: 5 minutes
  • In-match adaptation scenarios: 10 minutes (visualize being down a set, adjusting to opponent's changes)

  • Post-match reflection: 5 minutes (what worked, what to adapt)

  • Pressure Training (2x/week)

  • Practice with score simulations (e.g., always start at 0-30, 15-40, etc.)
  • Practice changing tactics based on hypothetical coaching instructions
  • Develop routines for challenging situations (wind, sun, noisy crowd)

docs.title: On-Court Application (3x/week, 45-60 minutes)
docs.text:
• Flexibility Under Fatigue
  • Play points immediately after suicide sprints: focus on maintaining technique

  • Shadow swings after planks: focus on maintaining range of motion

  • Adaptive Point Play

  • Practice changing grip/spin/trajectory mid-rally based on called-out instructions
  • Play points where you must use a different shot pattern every 3 shots

  • Practice playing with simulated injuries (e.g., favor one leg, limited shoulder rotation)

  • Match Simulations

  • Play practice sets with specific adaptation goals (e.g., must change strategy every game)
  • Play practice matches where coach can call for tactical changes mid-game

docs.title: Week 7-9 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Flexibility AM/PM + Tennis-Specific Elasticity AM + Mental Training PM + On-Court Application (light)
  • Tuesday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application AM (adaptive drills) + Tennis-Specific Elasticity PM
  • Wednesday: Flexibility AM/PM + Mental Training AM + Elastic Strength PM + On-Court Application (match sim)
  • Thursday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application PM (fatigue drills) + Tennis-Specific Elasticity AM
  • Friday: Flexibility AM/PM + Mental Training AM + Elastic Strength PM + On-Court Application (adaptive)
  • Saturday: Flexibility AM/PM + Match Simulation (90 min)
  • Sunday: Flexibility AM/PM + Active Recovery + Extended Mental Work (30 min)

docs.title: Goals: Peak flexibility and elasticity, maintain mental sharpness, prepare for competition
Peak Flexibility Maintenance (15-20 minutes daily)
docs.text:
• Morning Routine (10 minutes)
  • Flow sequence focused on areas needing most attention that day

  • Dynamic movements mimicking tennis motions: 5 minutes

  • Evening Routine (10 minutes)

  • Targeted PNF or static stretching for tight areas
  • Foam rolling as needed
  • Breathing and brief meditation: 3 minutes

docs.title: Tennis-Specific Power & Elasticity (2x/week, 15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Maintenance Focus (lower volume, maintain intensity)
  • Pogo jump variations: 2x20 seconds
  • Medicine ball throws (focus on explosiveness): 2x10 each type
  • Lateral bounds with quick feet: 2x12 each side

docs.title: Competition-Specific Mental Flexibility (Daily, 15-20 minutes)
docs.text:
• Pre-Match Routines (5 minutes)
  • Visualization of match start and early game plans

  • Breathing exercises to achieve optimal arousal level

  • In-Match Adaptation Practice (10-15 minutes)

  • Review common opponent patterns and develop countermoves
  • Practice mental routines for challenging situations (bad calls, crowd noise, injury timeouts)
  • Develop reset routines for between points and changeovers

docs.title: On-Court Application (2-3x/week, 60-90 minutes)
docs.text:
• Competition Simulation
  • Practice matches with full scoring and adherence to routines
  • Focus on maintaining flexibility and explosiveness throughout match

  • Practice making tactical adjustments based on match flow

  • Specific Skill Maintenance

  • Serve practice with focus on smooth, elastic motion
  • Groundstroke consistency with full range of motion
  • Movement drills emphasizing quick feet and recovery

docs.title: Week 10-12 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Flexibility AM/PM + Tennis-Specific Elasticity AM + Mental Training PM + On-Court Application (light technical)
  • Tuesday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application AM (match simulation) + Tennis-Specific Elasticity PM
  • Wednesday: Flexibility AM/PM + Mental Training AM + Light Elastic Maintenance PM + On-Court Application (adaptive drills)
  • Thursday: Flexibility AM/PM + On-Court Application PM (match simulation) + Tennis-Specific Elasticity AM
  • Friday: Flexibility AM/PM + Mental Training AM + Elastic Maintenance PM + On-Court Application (pre-match routine practice)
  • Saturday: Flexibility AM/PM + Match Simulation or Light Practice (depending on tournament schedule)
  • Sunday: Flexibility AM/PM + Recovery Focus (light yoga, swimming, walk) + Mental Visualization

docs.title: During Tournaments
docs.text:
• Daily Maintenance
  • Morning flexibility routine non-negotiable
  • Evening routine adjusted based on match length and fatigue

  • Use foam roller and massage ball as needed

  • Pre-Match

  • Dynamic warm-up incorporating mobility and activation
  • Focus on feeling loose and elastic rather than stretched

  • Brief visualization of game plan and adaptive strategies

  • Between Matches

  • Prioritize recovery: nutrition, hydration, sleep
  • Light mobility work if feeling stiff
  • Mental detachment: engage in non-tennis activities

docs.title: Daily Life Integration
docs.text:
• Posture Awareness
  • Set reminders to check posture throughout day
  • Practice sitting with hip hinge rather than slouching

  • Stand and move every 30-45 minutes during sedentary work

  • Breathing & Stress Management

  • Practice 4-7-8 breathing during stressful moments
  • Use box breathing before bed or during changeovers

  • Daily gratitude or positive reflection practice

  • Hydration & Nutrition for Elasticity

  • Maintain consistent hydration (electrolytes as needed)
  • Include collagen-rich foods or vitamin C for connective tissue health
  • Omega-3 fatty acids for joint inflammation management

docs.title: Weekly Metrics to Track
docs.text:
1. Morning Flexibility Score (1-10): Subjective rating of overall looseness upon waking
  2. Evening Recovery Score (1-10): Subjective rating of how well body recovered from day's activities
  3. Elasticity Feel (1-10): During explosive movements, how springy and responsive the body feels
  4. Mental Flexibility Score (1-10): Ability to adapt thinking and strategies when presented with new information

docs.title: Monthly Assessment
docs.text:
1. Flexibility Testing
  2. Sit-and-reach test
  3. Shoulder flexion/extension with strap
  4. Hip internal/external rotation (seated)
  5. Ankle dorsiflexion (knee to wall test)

  6. Trunk rotation (seated, arms across chest)

  7. Elasticity Testing

  8. Reactive strength index (drop jump height/contact time)
  9. 10-5 repeat hop test (bilateral and unilateral)

  10. Medicine ball throw distance for height (seated chest throw)

  11. On-Court Assessment

  12. Coach observation of movement efficiency and range of motion
  13. Video analysis of serve and groundstroke elasticity

  14. Match data: points won from extreme positions, recovery ability after long rallies

  15. Mental Assessment

  16. Self-reflection journal on adaptability in practice/matches
  17. Coach feedback on decision-making under changing conditions
  18. Ability to execute varied game plans in practice matches

docs.title: Beginner Focus (NTRP 2.5-3.5)
docs.text:
• Flexibility Focus: Basic range of motion development, consistency over intensity
  • Elasticity Focus: Low-intensity, focus on proper landing mechanics
  • Mental Focus: Simple routines, basic awareness of thoughts and emotions
  • Duration: May extend to 16-20 weeks with more gradual progression

docs.title: Intermediate Focus (NTRP 4.0-4.5)
docs.text:
• Standard progression as outlined above
  • Focus: Developing tennis-specific applications of flexibility and elasticity
  • Adjustment: Gradually increase intensity of elastic exercises

docs.title: Advanced Focus (NTRP 5.0+)
docs.text:
• Accelerated timeline: 8-10 week program possible with solid foundation
  • Focus: Maximizing elastic potential, advanced mental adaptability techniques
  • Adjustment: Incorporate sport-specific elastic tests, individualized mental performance plans

docs.title: Senior/Injury-Return Focus
docs.text:
• Reduced Impact Elasticity: Substitute jumps with step-touch movements, focus on controlled elasticity
  • Increased Recovery: Longer hold times in stretches, more frequent rest days
  • Focus: Maintaining functional range of motion, joint health, and mental sharpness
  • Equipment: Use of chairs for support, resistance bands for assisted movements

docs.title: Integration with Overall Game
docs.text:
• Serve Game: Use elastic serve motion to generate power with less muscular effort
  • Baseline Play: Develop ability to recover quickly from wide shots and maintain balance in extreme positions
  • Net Play: Use flexibility to handle low volleys and lobs effectively
  • Mental Game: Develop routines to stay present and adaptable regardless of score or circumstances

docs.title: Coach's Notes
docs.text:
• Individualization: Flexibility needs vary greatly based on individual structure, injury history, and playing style
  • Consistency Over Intensity: Daily consistency in flexibility work yields better results than occasional intense sessions
  • Video Feedback: Use delayed video or live feedback for immediate correction of movement patterns
  • Patience: Significant flexibility and elasticity changes take 8-12 weeks of consistent work
  • Fun and Engagement: Incorporate games and challenges to maintain motivation in flexibility work
  • Holistic Development: While flexibility is crucial, ensure balanced development of all tennis skills

docs.title: Safety Considerations
docs.text:
• Warm-up: Always complete light aerobic movement before static stretching
  • Breathing: Never hold breath during stretches; use exhaling to deepen stretches
  • Pain vs. Discomfort: Distinguish between discomfort (okay to work through) and sharp pain (stop immediately)
  • Joint Safety: Focus on muscular stretching, not forcing joints beyond natural range
  • Progressive Overload: Gradually increase stretch intensity and duration, not suddenly
  • Hydration: Well-hydrated muscles are more pliable and less prone to injury
  • Professional Guidance: Consider working with a qualified physical therapist or yoga instructor for personalized assessment

docs.title: References & Resources
docs.text:
• Video Study: Novak Djokovic match highlights (Australian Open, Wimbledon, US Open matches showcasing flexibility and defense)
  • Books: "Serve to Win" by Novak Djokovic, "The TB12 Method" by Tom Brady (for elasticity principles), various yoga and mobility texts
  • Coaching Aids: USPTA/PTR sports science materials, ATP/WTA player development resources
  • Technology: Motion capture systems, force plates, flexibility measurement tools if available
  • Expert Consultation: Consider working with a yoga instructor specializing in athletes, a sports massage therapist, and a mental performance coach

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This training program is designed to develop an all-court game modeled after Roger Federer, widely regarded as having one of the most complete and versatile games in tennis history. The program focuses on developing exceptional shot variety, court coverage, transition play, and the ability to dictate points from any position on the court—hallmarks of Federer's game that allowed him to dominate across all surfaces and eras.

docs.title: Program Overview
docs.text:
• Duration: 12 weeks (can be adjusted based on athlete level)
  • Frequency: 4 sessions per week
  • Session Length: 90-120 minutes
  • Equipment Needed: Tennis court, balls, targets (cones, zones), agility ladder, resistance bands, medicine balls, video analysis equipment
  • Prerequisites: Solid foundation in all basic strokes (forehand, backhand, serve, volley), basic footwork and court coverage understanding

docs.title: Philosophy & Approach
docs.text: Federer's game is built on: 1. Economy of Motion: Minimal wasted movement, maximum efficiency 2. Shot Variety: Ability to hit all spins, speeds, and trajectories 3. Court Positioning: Taking time away from opponent by stepping inside baseline 4. Transition Game: Seamless movement between baseline, mid-court, and net 5. Mental Calm: Maintaining composure and executing under pressure

docs.title: Goals: Develop spin variety, depth control, and basic transition movement
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Forehand Variety Development (25 minutes/session)
  • Flat drive: Focus on flat trajectory through contact
  • Topspin: Brush up the back of the ball for heavy spin
  • Slice: Under-spin with open racquet face
  • Inside-out/inside-in: Work on directional control from forehand side

  • Drill: Hit 10 balls of each type to specific targets, rotate through varieties

  • Backhand Versatility (20 minutes/session)

  • Develop both one-handed and two-handed options (if applicable)
  • Focus on aggressive topspin, neutral drive, and defensive slice
  • Practice handling high balls with one-handed backhand (if applicable)

  • Drill: Alternate between topspin and slice to same target

  • Serve Variety (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice flat, slice, and kick serves from same toss
  • Focus on disguising serve type until last possible moment

  • Drill: Serve to three locations (wide, body, T) with each serve type

  • Volley & Overhead (15 minutes/session)

  • Punch volley: Minimal backswing, punch through ball
  • Drop volley: Soft hands, absorb pace
  • Half-volley: Meet ball immediately after bounce
  • Overhead: Proper positioning and timing
  • Drill: Volley to volley with partner, alternating forehand/backhand

docs.title: Movement & Court Coverage
docs.text:
• Split Step & Recovery (15 minutes/session)
  • Practice split step timing to opponent's contact
  • Focus on quick first step in all directions
  • Recovery steps: crossover, shuffle, grapevine

  • Drill: Shadow movement to called out positions (wide forehand, wide backhand, short ball)

  • Baseline to Transition (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice moving forward after short balls
  • Develop "step in" mentality for attack opportunities
  • Drill: Coach feeds short ball, player moves in and hits approach shot

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Agility & Footwork
  • Ladder drills: Ickey shuffle, lateral runs, in-and-out (4 sets of 30 seconds)
  • Cone drills: T-drill, pro-agility, box drill (3 sets each direction)

  • Suicide sprints with tennis-specific movements (4 sets)

  • Core Stability & Rotation

  • Plank variations: front, side, reverse (3 sets of 45 seconds)
  • Russian twists with medicine ball: 3 sets of 20
  • Cable/pallof press: 3 sets of 12 each side

  • Rotational medicine ball throws: 3 sets of 15 each side

  • Explosive Power

  • Box jumps: 3 sets of 10
  • Medicine ball slams: 3 sets of 15
  • Broad jumps: 4 sets of 8

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Cross-Court Consistency (20 minutes)
  • Maintain deep, cross-court rallies with specific targets
  • Focus on consistency over power initially

  • Goal: 20+ ball rallies with 80%+ accuracy to target zone

  • Direction Change Drills (15 minutes)

  • Practice changing direction from crosscourt to down-the-line
  • Work on inside-out and inside-in forehand

  • Drill: Hit two crosscourt, then one down-the-line, repeat

  • Approach Shot Practice (15 minutes)

  • Practice hitting approach shots and following to net
  • Focus on placement over power
  • Drill: Serve and follow, or short ball approach and volley

docs.title: Week 1-3 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Stroke Variety + Agility (100 min)
  • Wednesday: Movement + Core (90 min)
  • Friday: Serve/Volley + Explosive (100 min)
  • Sunday: Match Play Application (90 min) - focus on implementing variety

docs.title: Goals: Develop ability to take time away from opponent, improve net play, enhance anticipation
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Taking Time Away (20 minutes/session)
  • Practice stepping inside baseline to hit balls on the rise
  • Develop "half-volley" groundstrokes for balls at feet
  • Work on taking serve returns early (especially second serves)

  • Drill: Coach feeds balls at varying depths, player must move in and hit before ball drops below knee height

  • Approach Shot Development (15 minutes/session)

  • Develop different approach shot types: flat, topspin, slice
  • Practice approaching to different court areas based on ball height and spin
  • Work on approach shot placement to set up easy volley

  • Drill: Serve and follow, or baseline rally until short ball, then approach and volley

  • Volley Placement & Touch (20 minutes/session)

  • Practice placing volleys to specific court areas (deep, angled, drop)
  • Develop reflex volleys for balls at body
  • Work on swing volleys for higher balls

  • Drill: Volley to target zones, alternating forehand/backhand

  • Passing Shot & Lob (15 minutes/session)

  • Develop passing shots down the line and crosscourt
  • Practice lobs offensively and defensively
  • Work on lob placement over specific court areas
  • Drill: Player at net, baseline player feeds balls to practice passing/lob

docs.title: Movement & Anticipation
docs.text:
• Recovery & Repositioning (15 minutes/session)
  • Practice recovering to optimal court position after each shot
  • Develop "recover to the middle" philosophy with adjustments
  • Work on recovering based on opponent's likely shot

  • Drill: Shadow recovery patterns after hitting to different court zones

  • Anticipation & Recognition (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice reading opponent's preparation to predict shot
  • Work on recognizing serve toss and grip for serve anticipation
  • Develop ability to read body positioning for shot selection
  • Drill: Video analysis of opponent patterns, then live practice calling out shot before contact

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Lateral Explosiveness
  • Lateral bounds: 4 sets of 15 each side
  • Shuffle to sprint: 4 sets of 20 yards

  • Resisted lateral walks with bands: 3 sets of 20 steps each direction

  • Reaction Speed

  • Ball drop reaction: Partner drops ball, you catch after one bounce (3 sets of 20)
  • Light-based reaction (if available): React to light cues

  • Mirror drill: Partner leads, you mirror movements (3 sets of 30 seconds)

  • Endurance & Recovery

  • Tempo runs: 20 minutes at moderate pace
  • Interval training: 30 seconds hard/90 seconds easy x 8
  • Active recovery: Light jogging, cycling, swimming

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Transition Point Play (25 minutes)
  • Play points where you must come to net after approach shot
  • Focus on constructing points to get to net

  • Drill: Serve and volley only, or baseline until short ball then come in

  • Half-Volley Drills (15 minutes)

  • Practice hitting half-volleys from different court positions
  • Work on both offensive and defensive half-volleys

  • Drill: Coach feeds balls at feet, player hits half-volley to target

  • Point Construction from Different Court Zones (20 minutes)

  • Practice constructing points from baseline, mid-court, and net
  • Work on using different shots to move opponent and create openings
  • Drill: Play points starting from specific court positions

docs.title: Week 4-6 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Tuesday: Transition Game + Lateral Explosiveness (100 min)
  • Thursday: Volley/Passing + Reaction (90 min)
  • Saturday: Match Play Transition Focus (100 min)
  • Sunday: Review & Light Practice (60 min)

docs.title: Phase 3: Match Play Integration & Mental Game (Weeks 7-9)
Goals: Integrate all-court game into match situations, develop mental routines, enhance tactical awareness
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Point Construction Patterns (20 minutes/session)
  • Develop go-to patterns: serve and forehand inside-out, approach and volley, etc.
  • Practice varying patterns based on opponent tendencies
  • Work on constructing points to exploit weaknesses

  • Drill: Play sets with specific point construction goals (e.g., every point must include approach shot)

  • Shot Selection Under Pressure (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice making correct shot choices in pressure situations
  • Work on choosing between aggressive and conservative options
  • Develop ability to change tactics mid-point based on opponent response

  • Drill: Play tiebreaks with coach feeding specific situations (break point, set point, etc.)

  • Adapting to Different Opponents (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice adjusting game plan based on opponent style
  • Work on specific strategies for baseliners, serve-volleyers, pushers, etc.
  • Develop ability to identify and exploit opponent weaknesses during warm-up

  • Drill: Play practice sets against different style partners, adjusting tactics each set

  • Mental Routines & Focus (10 minutes/session)

  • Develop pre-serve and pre-return routines
  • Practice between-points routines to stay focused and relaxed
  • Work on letting go of mistakes and staying present
  • Drill: Simulate stressful situations (down break point, serving for set) and practice routines

docs.title: Movement & Court Coverage
docs.text:
• Court Geometry & Angles (15 minutes/session)
  • Practice using angles to open up court
  • Work on recovering to cover angles effectively
  • Develop understanding of optimal court positioning for different shots

  • Drill: Hit angles and practice recovery, then play points focusing on angle creation

  • Defensive to Offensive Transitions (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice turning defense into offense with effective shots
  • Work on recognizing when to neutralize vs. attack
  • Develop ability to hit offensive shots from defensive positions
  • Drill: Play points starting in defensive position, must work back to neutral/offensive

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Sport-Specific Endurance
  • Tennis-specific intervals: 30 seconds sprint/90 seconds light jog (mimicking point/rest ratio) x 10
  • Suicide drills with tennis movements: sprint to net, backpedal to baseline, etc.

  • On-court suicides: sideline to sideline, net to baseline, etc.

  • Strength Maintenance

  • Focus on maintaining strength with lower volume
  • Compound movements: squats, lunges, push-ups, rows (3 sets of 12)

  • Core maintenance: planks, Russian twists, leg raises (3 sets of 30 seconds)

  • Flexibility & Mobility

  • Dynamic stretching before sessions
  • Static stretching after sessions (focus on hips, shoulders, spine)
  • Yoga or mobility work 2x per week

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Match Simulation (30 minutes)
  • Play practice sets and matches
  • Focus on implementing all-court game strategies

  • Track statistics: winners, unforced errors, net points won, approach shot success

  • Situational Practice (20 minutes)

  • Practice specific score situations: love-40, deuce, ad-in, ad-out, tiebreaks
  • Work on maintaining game plan under different score pressures

  • Drill: Play games starting at specific scores, must win to rotate

  • Video Review & Analysis (10 minutes)

  • Review match footage of your play
  • Compare to Federer's decision making and shot selection
  • Identify one tactical and one technical area to improve each week

docs.title: Week 7-9 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Point Construction + Sport-Specific Endurance (100 min)
  • Wednesday: Mental Routines + Strength Maintenance (90 min)
  • Friday: Match Simulation + Video Review (100 min)
  • Sunday: Practice Match (90 min) - full match with post-match analysis

docs.title: Goals: Refine all-court game, peak for competition, develop consistency under pressure
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Consistency Under Pressure (20 minutes/session)
  • Practice maintaining high percentage tennis in pressure situations
  • Work on reducing unforced errors during important points
  • Develop ability to stick to game plan even when not feeling "in the zone"

  • Drill: Play points where you lose point if you make unforced error

  • Shot Selection Refinement (15 minutes/session)

  • Fine-tune decision making based on opponent positioning and court geometry
  • Work on disguising intentions until last possible moment
  • Develop ability to change spin, speed, and direction from same preparation

  • Drill: Coach feeds ball, you must call out shot type before hitting (to ensure variety)

  • Specialty Shots & Trickery (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice drop shots, lobs, and trick shots for specific situations
  • Work on using variety to disrupt opponent rhythm
  • Develop ability to hit winners from defensive positions

  • Drill: Play points where you must attempt a specialty shot at least once per game

  • Match Preparation Routines (10 minutes/session)

  • Develop pre-match warm-up routine
  • Practice mental preparation and visualization
  • Work on routines between sets and during breaks
  • Drill: Simulate match day schedule with practice matches and recovery

docs.title: Movement & Anticipation
docs.text:
• Optimal Court Positioning (15 minutes/session)
  • Practice recovering to ideal position based on shot hit
  • Work on anticipating opponent's shot based on your own shot placement
  • Develop ability to take away opponent's angles

  • Drill: Play points where you must call out your recovery position before hitting

  • Reaction & Anticipation Refinement (15 minutes/session)

  • Continue refining anticipation skills
  • Work on reducing reaction time through better preparation
  • Develop ability to read subtle cues in opponent's preparation
  • Drill: Partner hides racquet until last moment, you must react to ball only

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Peak Maintenance
  • Reduce volume, maintain intensity
  • Focus on sharpness rather than fatigue
  • Maintain agility and reaction work

  • Keep strength work light to avoid soreness

  • Recovery & Regeneration

  • Prioritize sleep and nutrition
  • Incorporate massage, foam rolling, contrast baths
  • Active recovery: light swimming, cycling, yoga
  • Mental recovery: meditation, visualization, leisure activities

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Competition Simulation (30 minutes)
  • Play practice matches with full scoring and officiating
  • Simulate tournament conditions (warm-up, match, cool-down)
  • Focus on implementing competition game plan

  • Track detailed statistics and conduct post-match analysis

  • Specific Competition Preparation (20 minutes)

  • If preparing for specific tournament, practice on similar surface
  • Work on specific opponent tendencies if known
  • Develop contingency plans for different scenarios (wind, sun, surface speed)

  • Drill: Practice matches with simulated conditions (e.g., windy day with fans)

  • Mental Rehearsal & Visualization (10 minutes)

  • Visualize successful match execution
  • Practice positive self-talk and confidence building
  • Work on staying present and enjoying competition
  • Drill: Before practice match, spend 5 minutes visualizing successful performance

docs.title: Week 10-12 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Consistency + Peak Maintenance (90 min)
  • Wednesday: Specialty Shots + Recovery Focus (90 min)
  • Friday: Competition Simulation + Mental Rehearsal (100 min)
  • Sunday: Light Practice or Rest (60 min) - or practice match if competition soon

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 1-3)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Stroke Variety + Agility 100 min Wednesday Movement + Core 90 min Friday Serve/Volley + Explosive 100 min Sunday Match Play Application 90 min

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 4-6)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Tuesday Transition Game + Lateral Explosiveness 100 min Thursday Volley/Passing + Reaction 90 min Saturday Match Play Transition Focus 100 min Sunday Review & Light Practice 60 min

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 7-9)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Point Construction + Sport-Specific Endurance 100 min Wednesday Mental Routines + Strength Maintenance 90 min Friday Match Simulation + Video Review 100 min Sunday Practice Match 90 min

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 10-12)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Consistency + Peak Maintenance 90 min Wednesday Specialty Shots + Recovery Focus 90 min Friday Competition Simulation + Mental Rehearsal 100 min Sunday Light Practice or Rest 60 min

docs.title: Stroke Variety & Control
docs.text:
1. Spin Rainbow: Hit forehand with flat, topspin, slice in sequence to same target
  2. Direction Ladder: Hit to wide, body, T locations in progression
  3. Inside-Out/In Drill: Two crosscourt, one inside-out, repeat
  4. Slice Approach: Practice slice approach shots followed by volley
  5. Serve Variety: Same toss, different serve types to same location

docs.title: Movement & Court Coverage
docs.text:
1. Shadow to Called Positions: Move to called court position after shadow swing
  2. Recovery Patterns: After hitting shot, recover to optimal base position
  3. In-and-Out Steps: Practice moving forward for short balls, back for deep
  4. Diagonal Recovery: Hit shot, recover to cover likely return angle
  5. Split Step Timing: Jump rope or ladder work focusing on split step timing

docs.title: Transition & Net Play
docs.text:
1. Approach and Volley: Serve and follow, or baseline rally then approach
  2. Volley to Targets: Place volleys to specific zones (deep, angle, drop)
  3. Half-Volley Practice: Feed balls at feet, practice half-volley to targets
  4. Swing Volley: Practice swinging at higher balls
  5. Lob and Lob Return: Practice offensive lobs and defending against lobs

docs.title: Pressure & Match Play
docs.text:
1. Consistency Challenge: See how many balls you can keep in play with specific constraints
  2. Point Construction Game: Play points where you must follow a specific pattern
  3. Pressure Situations: Practice serving for match, facing break points, etc.
  4. Score Situation Games: Start games at specific scores (deuce, ad-in, etc.)
  5. Video Feedback Drill: Record play, review, implement one change next session

docs.title: Agility & Footwork Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 4 times per week
  • Intensity: High effort, short bursts (10-20 seconds)
  • Recovery: Full recovery between bouts (40-60 seconds)
  • Progression: Increase complexity (add racquet work, decision making) before duration

docs.title: Strength & Power Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 2-3 times per week
  • Intensity: Moderate (60-80% effort)
  • Volume: 2-3 sets of 8-15 repetitions
  • Focus: Functional movements, core stability, injury prevention

docs.title: Endurance Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: 2-3 times per week
  • Type: Interval-based mimicking tennis work-rest ratios
  • Example: 30 seconds high intensity/90 seconds active recovery x 8-10
  • On-Court: Suicides, ladder drills with racquet work

docs.title: Recovery Focus
docs.text:
• Frequency: Daily
  • Components: Stretching, foam rolling, hydration, nutrition, sleep
  • Active Recovery: 2-3 times per week (light swimming, cycling, yoga)

docs.title: Weekly Metrics to Track
docs.text:
1. Shot Variety Percentage: % of shots hit with different spins/speeds from same preparation
  2. Net Approach Success: % of approach shots won point or forced error
  3. Transition Points Won: % of points won when coming to net
  4. Court Coverage: Subjective rating of ability to reach wide balls (1-10)
  5. Unforced Error Rate: % of total shots that are unforced errors (goal: <15%)

docs.title: Monthly Assessment
docs.text:
1. Video Analysis: Compare technique and decision making to baseline video
  2. Match Statistics: Track performance in practice matches
  3. Physical Testing:
  4. Pro-agility time
  5. Vertical jump height
  6. Medicine ball throw distance (rotational and overhead)
  7. Plank hold time
  8. Tactical Awareness: Coach assessment of decision making in match situations
  9. Mental Game Rating: Self-rating on focus, composure, and adaptability (1-10)

docs.title: Beginner Focus (NTRP 2.5-3.5)
docs.text:
• Weeks 1-3: Extended focus on basic stroke mechanics and consistency
  • Weeks 4-6: Slower pace feeds, emphasis on making contact and basic movement
  • Weeks 7-9: Introduction to transition play with larger targets and slower pace
  • Weeks 10-12: Game-based situations, focus on consistency over variety

docs.title: Intermediate Focus (NTRP 4.0-4.5)
docs.text:
• Standard progression as outlined above
  • Emphasis: Developing ability to use variety strategically
  • Adjustment: Increase pace and complexity gradually

docs.title: Advanced Focus (NTRP 5.0+)
docs.text:
• Accelerated timeline: 8-10 week program possible
  • Emphasis: Tactical variations, pressure performance, and disguising intentions
  • Adjustment: Incorporate opponent-specific strategies and scouting reports

docs.title: Senior/Injury-Return Focus
docs.text:
• Reduced Impact: Substitute explosive movements with controlled steps
  • Increased Recovery: Longer rest intervals, additional recovery days
  • Focus: Precision, placement, and economical movement over explosiveness
  • Equipment: Use of softer balls, smaller court if needed

docs.title: Integration with Overall Game
docs.text:
• Serve Game: Use variety to keep opponent off balance and set up easy points
  • Baseline Play: Develop ability to neutralize and transition from defense to offense
  • Net Play: Develop touch and placement to finish points effectively
  • Mental Game: Develop routines to stay present and enjoy the process of constructing points

docs.title: Coach's Notes
docs.text:
• Individualization: Adjust based on player's physique, age, and natural tendencies (aggressor vs. defender)
  • Video Feedback: Use delayed video or live feedback for immediate correction
  • Patience: All-court game development takes time; expect 10-12 weeks for noticeable changes
  • Fun and Engagement: Incorporate games and challenges to maintain motivation
  • Holistic Development: All-court game is ideal but ensure balanced development of all skills

docs.title: Safety Considerations
docs.text:
• Warm-up: Always complete dynamic warm-up before intense movement work
  • Cool-down: Static stretching for hips, legs, shoulders, and back after sessions
  • Hydration: Maintain proper fluid intake, especially during intense sessions
  • Surface: Be aware of court conditions; slippery surfaces increase injury risk
  • Equipment: Use appropriate footwear with good lateral and multidirectional support

docs.title: References & Resources
docs.text:
• Video Study: Roger Federer match highlights (Wimbledon finals, Australian Open)
  • Books: "Roger Federer: The Biography" by Chris Bowers, "The Federer Biography" by Chris Bowers
  • Coaching Aids: USPTA/PTR all-court player development materials
  • Technology: Launch monitors, high-speed cameras for analysis if available
  • Philosophy Books: "The Inner Game of Tennis" by W. Timothy Gallwey (for mental aspects)

Program developed based on analysis of Roger Federer's all-court game, training methodologies, and match performance data. Adapt volume, intensity, and focus based on individual athlete needs, age, and competitive level. Consult with qualified tennis coach and fitness professional before beginning any intensive training program.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This training program is designed to develop the physical attributes and on-court movements that define Rafael Nadal's dominance, particularly his legendary topspin forehand, defensive sliding, and incredible endurance on clay courts. The program focuses on building explosive lower body strength, lateral mobility, core stability, and the specific movement patterns that allow Nadal to defend and counterpunch with exceptional effectiveness.

docs.title: Program Overview
docs.text:
• Duration: 12 weeks (can be adjusted based on athlete level)
  • Frequency: 4-5 sessions per week (mix of on-court and off-court training)
  • Session Length: 90-120 minutes
  • Equipment Needed: Tennis court, balls, agility ladder, cones, resistance bands, medicine balls, slide board (or smooth surface for sliding practice), foam roller, massage ball, video analysis equipment
  • Prerequisites: Solid foundation in basic tennis strokes, basic lateral movement comfort, no serious joint limitations (consult with sports physician if needed)

docs.title: Philosophy & Approach
docs.text: Nadal's physical game is built on: 1. Explosive Lower Body Power: For explosive first steps and recovery steps 2. Lateral Mobility & Sliding Ability: Unique ability to slide and recover on clay and other surfaces 3. Core & Rotational Strength: For generating massive topspin and stabilizing during extreme stretches 4. Exceptional Endurance & Recovery: Ability to maintain high intensity for hours 5. Injury Prevention & Longevity Focus: Emphasis on shoulder, knee, and ankle health

docs.title: Goals: Develop proper movement mechanics, build foundational strength, introduce sliding basics
Movement & Footwork
docs.text:
• Lateral Movement Drills (20 minutes/session)
  • Ladder drills: lateral shuffles, in-and-outs, crossover steps (4 sets of 30 seconds)
  • Cone drills: zig-zag, T-drill with lateral emphasis (3 sets each direction)

  • Shadow sliding practice on appropriate surface (focus on form, not speed initially)

  • Split Step & Recovery Timing (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice split step timing to various ball feeds
  • Focus on quick first step in all directions, especially laterally
  • Recovery steps: crossover recovery, backpedal to shuffle combination

docs.title: Strength & Power
docs.text:
• Lower Body Explosiveness (20 minutes/session)
  • Squat jumps: 4 sets of 8
  • Lateral bounds: 4 sets of 10 each side
  • Box jumps: 3 sets of 8

  • Broad jumps: 3 sets of 8

  • Posterior Chain Development (15 minutes/session)

  • Deadlifts (light to moderate, focus on form): 3 sets of 8
  • Romanian deadlifts: 3 sets of 10
  • Glute bridges: 3 sets of 15
  • Hamstring curls (machine or ball): 3 sets of 12

docs.title: Core & Stability
docs.text:
• Rotational Core (15 minutes/session)
  • Russian twists with medicine ball: 3 sets of 20
  • Cable/pallof press: 3 sets of 12 each side
  • Rotational medicine ball throws: 3 sets of 15 each side

  • Plank with shoulder taps: 3 sets of 45 seconds

  • Anti-Rotation & Stability (10 minutes/session)

  • Bird-dog: 3 sets of 12 each side
  • Dead bug: 3 sets of 15 each side
  • Side plank variations: 3 sets of 30 seconds each side

docs.title: On-Court Application
docs.text:
• Forehand Technique Foundation (20 minutes/session)
  • Focus on grip (semi-western to western) for topspin generation
  • Practice low-to-high swing path

  • Drill: Crosscourt forehand consistency (aim for 20+ ball rallies)

  • Movement to Ball & Recovery (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice moving to wide forehand and backhand, then recovering to center
  • Emphasize outside foot lead for lateral movement

docs.title: Week 1-3 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Movement Foundations + Lower Body Power (90 min)
  • Wednesday: Core Stability + Forehand Technique (90 min)
  • Friday: Lateral Movement + Recovery Patterns (90 min)
  • Sunday: Integrated On-Court Practice (90 min) - focus on movement and forehand

docs.title: Goals: Develop sliding technique, improve defensive capabilities, build endurance base
Movement & Sliding
docs.text:
• Sliding Technique Mastery (25 minutes/session)
  • Practice sliding on appropriate surface (clay court ideal, or use slide boards/socks on hard court)
  • Focus on: proper foot placement (lead foot slides, back foot pushes), body position low, recovery after slide

  • Drills: slide to wide forehand and recover, slide to wide backhand and recover

  • Defensive Movement Patterns (20 minutes/session)

  • Recovery from extreme widths: practice sliding far wide and recovering with crossover steps
  • Defensive lobs and lob recovery: move back, hit defensive lob, recover forward
  • Drill: Coach hits wide balls, player slides, recovers, and hits controlled return

docs.title: Strength & Power
docs.text:
• Explosive Lateral Power (20 minutes/session)
  • Lateral bounds with resistance bands: 4 sets of 8 each side
  • Lateral sled pushes/drags (if available): 4 sets of 20 yards

  • Skater jumps: 4 sets of 10 each side

  • Posterior Chain & Glute Focus (15 minutes/session)

  • Hip thrusts: 4 sets of 10
  • Single-leg Romanian deadlifts: 3 sets of 8 each leg
  • Lateral band walks: 3 sets of 20 steps each direction

docs.title: Core & Rotational Power
docs.text:
• Rotational Power Development (20 minutes/session)
  • Medicine ball rotational throws (wall or partner): 4 sets of 12 each side
  • Cable woodchoppers (high to low and low to high): 3 sets of 12 each direction

  • Russian twists with extended arms: 3 sets of 20

  • Anti-Extension Core (10 minutes/session)

  • Ab wheel rollouts: 3 sets of 10
  • Pallof press with iso-hold: 3 sets of 20 seconds each side
  • Hanging leg raises: 3 sets of 15

docs.title: On-Court Application
docs.text:
• Defensive Forehand Development (20 minutes/session)
  • Practice hitting heavy topspin forehands from defensive positions
  • Focus on generating spin even when stretched wide

  • Drill: Coach feeds wide balls, player hits heavy topspin forehand crosscourt

  • Point Construction from Defense (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice using defensive shots to neutralize and regain court position
  • Work on transitioning from defense to neutral with high, deep balls

docs.title: Week 4-6 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Tuesday: Sliding Technique + Lateral Power (90 min)
  • Thursday: Defensive Movement + Core Power (90 min)
  • Saturday: Integrated Defensive Play (90 min) - focus on sliding and recovery
  • Sunday: Match Play Simulation (90 min) - implement defensive skills

docs.title: Goals: Develop exceptional endurance, maintain explosiveness under fatigue, refine sliding under match conditions
Endurance & Conditioning
docs.text:
• Tennis-Specific Endurance Intervals (25 minutes/session)
  • Suicide sprints with tennis movements: 8-10 repetitions
  • On-court: sideline to sideline sprints with shadow strokes: 6-8 sets

  • Shuttle runs with directional changes: 6 sets of 30 seconds

  • High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) (20 minutes/session)

  • 30 seconds all-out effort (sprints, burpees, mountain climbers)/90 seconds active recovery x 8-10
  • Court suicides with racket: sprint to net, touch net, backpedal to baseline x 6-8

docs.title: Strength Maintenance & Power
docs.text:
• Maintenance Strength (15 minutes/session)
  • Squats: 3 sets of 8 (moderate weight)
  • Deadlifts: 3 sets of 6

  • Lunges (walking or stationary): 3 sets of 10 each leg

  • Explosive Maintenance (10 minutes/session)

  • Box jumps: 3 sets of 6
  • Med ball slams: 3 sets of 12
  • Lateral bounds: 3 sets of 8 each side

docs.title: Core & Injury Prevention
docs.text:
• Core Endurance (15 minutes/session)
  • Plank variations: 3 sets of 60 seconds
  • Side plank with hip dips: 3 sets of 15 each side

  • Hollow body hold: 3 sets of 45 seconds

  • Injury Prevention Focus (10 minutes/session)

  • Eccentric heel drops (Achilles): 3 sets of 15
  • External rotations with bands (shoulder): 3 sets of 20
  • Scapular wall slides: 3 sets of 15
  • Ankle mobility work: 5 minutes daily

docs.title: On-Court Application
docs.text:
• Sliding Under Fatigue (20 minutes/session)
  • Practice sliding and recovery after intense point play

  • Drill: Play 2-point games, immediately after each point perform slide and recovery drill

  • Defensive to Offensive Transitions (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice turning defensive slides into offensive opportunities
  • Work on hitting aggressive shots immediately after recovery slide

docs.title: Week 7-9 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Endurance Intervals + Maintenance Strength (90 min)
  • Wednesday: HIIT + Core Endurance (90 min)
  • Friday: Sliding Under Fatigue + Explosive Maintenance (90 min)
  • Sunday: Extended Match Play (120 min) - focus on maintaining intensity

docs.title: Goals: Integrate all physical components into match play, peak for competition, maintain health
Competition Preparation
docs.text:
• Match Simulation Conditioning (25 minutes/session)
  • Play practice sets with specific physical focuses (e.g., every third point must include a slide recovery)

  • Practice maintaining technique and movement intensity throughout long sets

  • Peaking & Tapering (Weeks 11-12)

  • Week 10: High volume, moderate intensity
  • Week 11: Moderate volume, high intensity
  • Week 12: Low volume, maintenance intensity (focus on sharpness and recovery)

docs.title: Maintenance & Recovery
docs.text:
• Active Recovery Sessions (2-3 times/week)
  • Light swimming, cycling, or yoga (30-45 minutes)

  • Foam rolling and mobility work (15-20 minutes daily)

  • Injury Prevention Maintenance (Daily)

  • Continue eccentric heel drops, external rotations, scapular work
  • Regular massage or self-myofascial release on key areas (calves, quads, hips, shoulders)

docs.title: On-Court Application
docs.text:
• Comprehensive Match Play (30 minutes/session)
  • Implement all learned physical skills in match situations

  • Focus on using physical advantages to construct points and wear down opponents

  • Mental-Physical Integration (15 minutes/session)

  • Practice maintaining physical intensity while managing match pressure
  • Develop routines for quick recovery between points and games

docs.title: Week 10-12 Schedule Example
docs.text:
• Monday: Match Simulation + Active Recovery (90 min)
  • Wednesday: Technical Maintenance + Injury Prevention (90 min)
  • Friday: Peaking Work + Mental-Physical Integration (90 min)
  • Sunday: Light Practice or Match Play (60-90 min) - adjust based on competition schedule

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 1-6 Example)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Movement Foundations + Lower Body Power 90 min Wednesday Core Stability + Forehand Technique 90 min Friday Lateral Movement + Recovery Patterns 90 min Sunday Integrated On-Court Practice 90 min

docs.title: Sample Weekly Schedule (Weeks 7-9 Example)
docs.text: Day Focus Duration Monday Endurance Intervals + Maintenance Strength 90 min Wednesday HIIT + Core Endurance 90 min Friday Sliding Under Fatigue + Explosive Maintenance 90 min Sunday Extended Match Play 120 min

docs.title: Sliding & Recovery
docs.text:
1. Slide and Recover: Slide to wide forehand, hit recovery step, recover to center
  2. Slide to Shadow Stroke: Slide wide, immediately hit shadow forehand/backhand during recovery
  3. Defensive Lob Recovery: Hit defensive lob, immediately recover forward for next shot
  4. Slide Direction Changes: Slide wide, recover, slide to opposite wide (develops quick feet)

docs.title: Explosive Power
docs.text:
1. Lateral Bound to Catch: Bound laterally, catch medicine ball thrown at peak
  2. Box Jump to Immediate Sprint: Explode onto box, immediately sprint 5 yards
  3. Resisted Lateral Walks: Band around ankles, walk laterally maintaining tension

docs.title: Endurance & Tennis-Specific
docs.text:
1. Suicide Sprints with Shadow Strokes: Sprint to line, shadow stroke, sprint back
  2. Corner-to-Corner Sprints: Sprint from one corner to opposite diagonal corner
  3. Continuous Point Play: Play points for 5 minutes straight, focus on movement quality

docs.title: Lower Body Power & Explosiveness
docs.text:
• Frequency: 3-4 times per week
  • Intensity: High effort, low reps (6-10 reps for power movements)
  • Recovery: Full recovery between sets (2-3 minutes)
  • Progression: Increase complexity (add direction changes, unstable surfaces) before volume

docs.title: Lateral Mobility & Sliding
docs.text:
• Frequency: 4-5 times per week (include some form of lateral work daily)
  • Focus: Quality over quantity, emphasize proper technique
  • Surface Progression: Start on slide boards/socks, progress to appropriate court surface
  • Volume: Short bursts (10-20 seconds) with full recovery

docs.title: Core & Rotational Strength
docs.text:
• Frequency: 3-4 times per week
  • Type: Mix of anti-rotation, rotational power, and endurance work
  • Progression: Increase resistance before increasing volume or duration

docs.title: Endurance & Conditioning
docs.text:
• Frequency: 2-3 times per week (in addition to tennis practice)
  • Type: Interval-based mimicking tennis work-rest ratios (typically 1:3 to 1:5)
  • Examples:
  • 30 seconds hard/90 seconds easy x 8-10
  • 15 seconds all-out/45 seconds easy x 10-12
  • Extended match simulation: play points for 10-15 minutes with limited rest

docs.title: Weekly Metrics to Track
docs.text:
1. Lateral Movement Time: Time to move laterally 5 meters and back (goal: improve by 10-15%)
  2. Sliding Distance: Maximum controlled slide distance on appropriate surface
  3. Vertical Jump Height: Measure via jump mat or wall tap (goal: maintain or improve)
  4. Lateral Bound Distance: Distance covered in 3 consecutive bounds (goal: improve)
  5. Perceived Exertion During Match Play: Rate 1-10 scale during practice sets

docs.title: Monthly Assessment
docs.text:
1. Movement Screening: Lateral movement assessment, sliding technique video analysis
  2. Strength Testing:
  3. Squat jump height
  4. Lateral bound distance
  5. Medicine ball throw distance (rotational)
  6. Endurance Testing:
  7. 300-yard shuttle time
  8. Ability to maintain intensity in 15-minute point play simulation
  9. Flexibility & Mobility:
  10. Hip internal/external rotation
  11. Ankle dorsiflexion
  12. Shoulder internal/external rotation (critical for tennis shoulder health)
  13. Injury Markers: Monitor for joint soreness, particularly knees, ankles, shoulders

docs.title: Beginner Focus (NTRP 2.5-3.5)
docs.text:
• Weeks 1-3: Extended focus on basic movement patterns and sliding fundamentals (use socks on smooth surface)
  • Weeks 4-6: Slower pace feeds, emphasis on making contact while moving
  • Weeks 7-9: Introduction to sliding with direction recovery at 50% speed
  • Weeks 10-12: Game-based situations, focus on consistent movement over explosiveness

docs.title: Intermediate Focus (NTRP 4.0-4.5)
docs.text:
• Standard progression as outlined above
  • Emphasis: Developing ability to slide effectively and recover for next shot
  • Adjustment: Increase sliding distance and speed gradually

docs.title: Advanced Focus (NTRP 5.0+)
docs.text:
• Accelerated timeline: 8-10 week program possible
  • Emphasis: High-intensity sliding under fatigue, explosive recovery
  • Adjustment: Incorporate opponent-specific movement patterns and scouting

docs.title: Senior/Injury-Return Focus
docs.text:
• Reduced Impact: Substitute explosive jumps with step movements, reduce slide distance
  • Increased Recovery: Longer rest intervals, additional recovery days
  • Focus: Precise movement, efficient recovery steps, injury prevention
  • Equipment: Use of slide aids if needed, softer surfaces if available

docs.title: Integration with Overall Game
docs.text:
• Serve Game: Use powerful leg drive to enhance serve speed and placement
  • Baseline Play: Develop ability to slide wide, recover, and hit aggressive shots
  • Defensive Play: Use sliding to extend points and turn defense into offense
  • Net Play: Use explosive first steps to cover lobs and passing shots
  • Mental Game: Develop confidence in physical abilities to take risks and extend points

docs.title: Coach's Notes
docs.text:
• Individualization: Adjust based on player's injury history, particularly knees and ankles
  • Surface Specificity: If player primarily plays on hard or grass, adjust sliding volume accordingly
  • Video Feedback: Use delayed video or live feedback for immediate correction of sliding technique
  • Patience: Developing elite-level movement and sliding takes consistent practice; expect 8-12 weeks for noticeable changes
  • Fun and Engagement: Incorporate games and challenges (e.g., sliding accuracy contests) to maintain motivation
  • Holistic Development: Physical excellence is crucial but ensure balanced development of all skills

docs.title: Safety Considerations
docs.text:
• Warm-up: Always complete dynamic warm-up before intense movement or sliding work (10-15 minutes)
  • Cool-down: Static stretching for hips, legs, shoulders, and back after sessions (10-15 minutes)
  • Hydration: Maintain proper fluid intake, especially during intense sessions and in heat
  • Surface: Be aware of court conditions; ensure appropriate sliding surface to prevent joint strain
  • Footwear: Use appropriate tennis shoes with good lateral support; consider specific clay court shoes if sliding extensively
  • Joint Monitoring: Pay attention to knee and ankle feedback; modify sliding volume if joint pain occurs
  • Shoulder Health: Given Nadal's extreme western grip and high biceps load, monitor shoulder and elbow closely

docs.title: References & Resources
docs.text:
• Video Study: Rafael Nadal match highlights (French Open finals, Davis Cup matches)
  • Books: "Rafa: My Story" by Rafael Nadal, tennis training and conditioning texts
  • Coaching Aids: USPTA/PTR clay court specialist materials, Nadal's academy training principles
  • Technology: GPS trackers, accelerometers, high-speed cameras for movement analysis if available
  • Expert Consultation: Consider working with a strength and conditioning coach familiar with tennis demands

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This training program is designed to develop a serve modeled after Pete Sampras, widely regarded as having one of the greatest serves in tennis history. The program focuses on developing explosive power, pinpoint accuracy, variety, and the ability to serve effectively under pressure—hallmarks of Sampras's serve that helped him win 14 Grand Slam titles.

docs.title: Program Overview
docs.text:
• Duration: 12 weeks (can be adjusted based on athlete level)
  • Frequency: 3-4 sessions per week
  • Session Length: 60-90 minutes
  • Equipment Needed: Tennis court, balls, targets (cones, zones), radar gun (optional but recommended), video analysis equipment
  • Prerequisites: Proper serving grip (continental or eastern backhand grip), basic service motion fundamentals

docs.title: Goals: Establish proper technique, develop consistent toss, build foundational strength
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Toss Consistency Drills (15 minutes daily)
  • Toss and catch practice (no swing) - 50 tosses per session
  • Target toss to specific heights and positions (12 o'clock for flat, slightly right for slice, slightly left for kick)

  • Video analysis of toss placement and consistency

  • Motion Breakdown (20 minutes)

  • Trophy position drills (holding the trophy position for 5-10 seconds)
  • Trophy to trophy swings (no ball) focusing on smooth motion
  • Shadow swings with focus on knee bend and coil/uncoil

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Explosive Leg Drive
  • Squat jumps: 3 sets of 10
  • Box jumps: 3 sets of 8

  • Lunges with twist: 3 sets of 12 each leg

  • Core Stability

  • Plank variations: 3 sets of 45-60 seconds
  • Russian twists: 3 sets of 20

  • Hanging leg raises: 3 sets of 15

  • Shoulder Stability

  • External rotations with band: 3 sets of 15 each side
  • Scapular retractions: 3 sets of 15
  • Wall slides: 3 sets of 10

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Serve to Targets (20 minutes)
  • Deuce court: Wide, body, T targets
  • Ad court: Wide, body, T targets
  • Goal: 60% accuracy to each zone
  • Start at 50% power, focus on placement

docs.title: Goals: Increase serve speed, develop kinetic chain efficiency, add variety
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Platform vs. Platform Stance Work (10 minutes)
  • Practice both stances to determine optimal for power vs. consistency

  • Video comparison of hip and shoulder rotation

  • Pronation Drills (15 minutes)

  • Towel snap exercises (snap towel downward with pronation)
  • Racquet pronation exercises from trophy position

  • "Snap" focus on contact point

  • Toss Variety (10 minutes)

  • Practice tossing for different serves (flat, slice, kick) from same motion
  • Hide serve type until last possible moment

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Explosive Power
  • Medicine ball slams: 4 sets of 10
  • Power cleans (light weight): 3 sets of 8

  • Broad jumps: 4 sets of 8

  • Rotational Power

  • Medicine ball rotational throws: 3 sets of 12 each side
  • Cable woodchoppers: 3 sets of 12 each side
  • Russian twists with weight: 3 sets of 20

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Speed & Accuracy Ladder (25 minutes)
  • Start at 70% max speed, aim for 80% accuracy to targets
  • Increase speed by 5% each successful set of 10 serves
  • Decrease speed if accuracy drops below 70%

  • Track speed with radar gun if available

  • Serve Variety Practice (15 minutes)

  • 20 first serves flat, 20 slice, 20 kick (alternating)
  • Focus on maintaining same toss and motion for all serves

docs.title: Goals: Develop ability to serve under fatigue and pressure, refine second serve
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Second Serve Development (20 minutes)
  • Kick serve specialization: focus on high bounce and spin
  • Slice serve for wide angles

  • Practice second serve placement under simulated pressure

  • Toss Under Pressure (10 minutes)

  • Practice toss with distractions (noise, movement)
  • Serve after physical exertion (sprints, jumping jacks)

docs.title: Physical Conditioning
docs.text:
• Endurance & Recovery
  • Interval sprints: 8 x 400m with 90-second rest
  • Suicide sprints: 6 sets

  • Agility ladder drills: 20 minutes

  • Shoulder Endurance

  • Light dumbbell raises: 3 sets of 20 (front, lateral, rear)
  • Band pull-aparts: 3 sets of 20
  • Scapular push-ups: 3 sets of 15

docs.title: Practice Application
docs.text:
• Pressure Serving Games (30 minutes)
  • "Break Point Serve": Serve for game at 30-40 or 40-Ad (ad-in or ad-out)
  • "Hold Serve Under Fatigue": Serve after sprinting baseline to baseline 10 times

  • "Consecutive Targets": Hit 10 serves in a row to same target, restart if miss

  • Match Simulation Serving (15 minutes)

  • Practice serving at 0-0, 15-30, 30-30, advantage points
  • Track first serve percentage under simulated pressure

docs.title: Goals: Integrate serve into overall game, develop patterns, refine tactical usage
Technical Work
docs.text:
• Serve & Follow (15 minutes)
  • Practice serving and immediately moving to net (for serve-and-volley)
  • Practice serving and staying back (for baseline play)

  • Focus on split-step timing after serve

  • Serve Patterns (15 minutes)

  • Develop serving patterns based on opponent tendencies
  • Practice serving to weaknesses (e.g., wide to backhand, then forehand pass)
  • Work on serving patterns to set up forehand inside-out
